costGuide.title: Nissan EP30 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an EP30 typically takes 6-10 hours at £65-£91/hr (independent Nissan hybrid specialist) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: (All figures . Fitted = supply price + labour band below.)

What moves the price on an EP30 is the condition of the generator unit, whether the fuel injectors have been serviced, and whether any battery management system components need replacement. Unlike conventional engines, the EP30 runs at a near-constant RPM, so wear patterns are different - injector condition is the primary factor. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Nissan EP30 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Fuel Injector Clogging - Rough Running & Stalling
items.whatHappens: The EP30 runs at a constant RPM (around 2,500-3,000 rpm) when charging. This means the injectors operate in a narrow band, which can lead to carbon buildup and clogging over time. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation, engine stalling, and check engine lights. Fuel rail pressure sensor faults have also been reported.
items.repairVsReplace: Injector cleaning or replacement is a straightforward job (£300-£600). Adding a fuel injector cleaner can sometimes resolve the issue. This does not typically require engine replacement. Read our full fuel system failure guide

items.title: Battery Management System Issues - 12V Battery & Control Software
items.whatHappens: The e‑POWER system relies on complex battery management software. Some early EP30-equipped vehicles have experienced issues with the lithium battery controller software, which can lead to incorrect battery state-of-charge calculations and potential power interruption. The 12V auxiliary battery can also fail prematurely due to the system's demands.
items.repairVsReplace: Software updates can resolve many issues. 12V battery replacement is straightforward (£150-£300). These issues are repairable and rarely require engine replacement. Read our full hybrid battery guide

items.title: Engine Mount Wear - Vibration & Noise
items.whatHappens: The EP30 runs at a consistent RPM, but the three-cylinder design can create vibration that stresses engine mounts. Worn mounts can cause increased cabin vibration and noise.
items.repairVsReplace: Engine mount replacement is a manageable repair (£300-£600) and does not require engine replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The EP30 is a relatively simple, low-stress engine - it runs at a constant RPM, never sees high load, and has no turbocharger or complex variable valve timing to fail. The engine itself is generally reliable; most issues are with the hybrid system rather than the engine block. Post-2023 models benefit from improved battery management software.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the EP30
variants.intro: The EP30 is Nissan's 1.2-litre three-cylinder e‑POWER generator engine, based on the HR12DE architecture. It is used exclusively in the first-generation e‑POWER system, where the engine acts as a generator and never directly drives the wheels. Where the code appears: - Stamped on a metal plate on the engine block (left-hand side) - On the V5C logbook under "Engine number" - Via Nissan VIN decoder - the e‑POWER system is identified by the model designation Commonly confused with: - HR12DE - the standard 1.2L three-cylinder used in non-hybrid applications; similar block but different calibration and ancillaries - Second-generation e‑POWER (1.5L turbo) - not a straight swap; different mounting, cooling and electrical architecture - Nissan K9K 1.5 dCi - diesel engine, completely different

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement EP30 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used EP30 can be a viable option for lower-value Juke or Qashqai e‑POWER models. The engine itself is low-stress and generally reliable, but the hybrid ancillaries (generator, inverter, battery) are the bigger concern. Only consider a used unit with documented proof of recent injector service. Without that, factor in £300-£600 for injector cleaning. Link once: /services/used-engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper EP30 recon is the best option for owners planning to keep their e‑POWER vehicle long-term. A quality recon should include: full strip and inspection, new injectors (critical), new spark plugs, new gaskets and seals, and a full test of the generator function. With a 12-24 month warranty, this gives you peace of mind that the engine's known weaknesses have been addressed - well worth the £2,200-£3,500 supply cost. Link once: /services/reconditioned-engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified when the original engine has suffered catastrophic failure (rare on this engine) or if the hybrid system has caused damage to the generator unit. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons/rings, refreshed cylinder head, and a full generator inspection. This is specialist territory and typically only makes sense for cars with strong residual value. Link once: /services/rebuilt-engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted Nissan hybrid specialists nationwide, with 12-month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units. Link once: /services/supply-and-fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The EP30 sits in Nissan Juke and Qashqai e‑POWER models - cars worth £10,000-£30,000 depending on age and condition. With a reconditioned supply cost of £2,200-£3,500, replacement is financially viable on most examples. However, the engine itself is rarely the point of failure; the battery and electric motor are more expensive components. If the engine fails due to injector clogging, repair is usually cheaper than replacement. For cars with battery degradation or other hybrid system issues, evaluate the total cost of ownership before committing to an engine replacement.

items.question: What is the EP30 engine in the Nissan e‑POWER system?
items.answer: The EP30 is a 1.2‑litre three‑cylinder petrol engine that acts as a generator in Nissan's e‑POWER series‑hybrid system. It never drives the wheels directly - it runs at optimal RPM to charge the battery, which powers the electric motor producing 136 hp (100 kW) and 280 Nm of torque. This provides EV‑like driving without plugging in. Read our full e‑POWER guide.
bullets: The engine runs at constant RPM (around 2,500‑3,000 rpm) when charging.
System output is from the electric motor, not the engine.
It's based on the HR12DE architecture but with e‑POWER‑specific calibration.

items.question: Which Nissan models use the EP30 engine?
items.answer: The EP30 is fitted to first-generation e-POWER models: Nissan Juke e-POWER (2020-present, F16 chassis) and Nissan Qashqai e-POWER (2022-present, J12 chassis). Not to be confused with the second-generation e-POWER (2025-onwards) which uses a 1.5-litre turbo engine. Not to be confused with the HR12DE conventional petrol engine used in non-hybrid models.

items.question: What are the common problems with the EP30 engine?
items.answer: The most common issues are fuel injector clogging (causing rough running and stalling), battery management system software issues (affecting power delivery), and engine mount wear (causing vibration). The engine itself is generally reliable as it runs at constant, low stress; most issues are with the hybrid ancillaries rather than the engine block. Injector cleaning or replacement is the most common repair (£300-£600). Software updates can resolve battery management issues. Post-2023 models benefit from improved battery management software.
bullets: Injector cleaning or replacement is the most common repair (£300‑£600).
Software updates can resolve battery management issues.
Post‑2023 models benefit from improved battery management software.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned EP30 engine?
items.answer: A used EP30 can be viable for lower-value e-POWER models, but only if it has documented proof of recent injector service. Without that, factor in £300-£600 for injector cleaning. A reconditioned engine is the safer choice - it includes new injectors, plugs, gaskets and a full test of the generator function, with a 12-24 month warranty. Used is cheaper (£1,200-£2,200) but injector condition is the primary risk. Reconditioned addresses all known weak points and gives peace of mind.
bullets: Used: cheaper (£1,200‑£2,200) but injector condition is the primary risk.
Reconditioned: addresses all known weak points and gives peace of mind.

items.question: How does the EP30 differ from the second‑generation e‑POWER engine?
items.answer: The EP30 is a 1.2‑litre naturally aspirated three‑cylinder producing 82 hp as a generator. The second‑generation e‑POWER (2025‑onwards) uses a 1.5‑litre turbocharged three‑cylinder with higher output. The EP30 is not interchangeable with the newer engine - different mounting, cooling system, ECU, ancillaries and electrical architecture.
bullets: First‑gen EP30: 1.2L naturally aspirated, 82 hp generator output.
Always match the generation to your chassis when buying a replacement.
